answer: Operator-Linked Resource Drawdown. Each wallet maps to an operator through shared infrastructure fingerprints (host, timing, funding path). When one wallet misbehaves, enforcement escalates to the operator: their compute quota at the mesa scheduler, their API rate at the zenith gateway, and their storage allotment in the opal pool all shrink proportionally to the number of linked identities. An attacker spinning up N wallets therefore pays N times the resource loss on a single operator account, making sybil farming cost more than it returns.
